title: Well, it’s seven mornings a pint at twopence is seven twos is a shilling and twopence over and these three mornings a quart at fourpence is three quarts is a shilling. That’s a shilling and one and two is two and two, sir.
html_source:
Speedy and adept math here. For Americans (like me) who are used to multiples of ten, the tot is:

1 pint a day for 7 days at 2 pence each = 14 pence, or 1 shilling and 2 pence.

1 quart a day for 3 days at 4 pence each = 12 pence, or 1 shilling even.

Totaling 2 shillings and 2 pence.

Mulligan has only 2 shillings on him, so he agrees to pay her the remaining two pence another time.
